newsitem.title: NORWAY: European countries sign Hebron observer agreement.
newsitem.headline: European countries sign Hebron observer agreement.

text.p: Six European countries formally agreed on Thursday to increase the number of observers in the West Bank town of Hebron, most of which was handed over to Palestinian rule by Israel two weeks ago.

A memorandum of understanding was signed by diplomats from Norway, Denmark, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland and Turkey in the government guest house where Israel and the Palestinian Liberation Organisation initialled the Oslo peace pact in 1993.

"This is a historic moment because three and a half years ago, in this very room, the Oslo agreement was initialled in secrecy by representatives of Israel and PLO," Norwegian junior foreign ministry Jan Egeland, one of the architects of the landmark peace pact, said after the ceremony.

Israeli troops withdrew from 80 percent of Hebron -- a volatile town of 100,000 Arabs and 400 Jews -- on January 17 after 10 months of acrimonious talks between the two sides focused on security issues.

Under the redeployment deal, about 150 international observers and administrators will join 30 Norwegians stationed in the town since last May as the Temporary International Presence in Hebron (TIPH).
"I think this temporary international presence in Hebron is historic also because it shows the interest of the international community in backing the peace process," Egeland said.
"And it shows that the parties have managed to reach agreement on very important measures for a continuation of the peace process," he added.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat bowed to U.S. political pressure in mid-January to clinch the long-delayed accord.
Egeland said all observers would be in place in a few weeks.
Unarmed, they have no military function. Their mandate is to record and report breaches of human rights. The mission is supposed to last three months, but can be extended by another three months.
The Hebron agreement includes Israeli pledges for additional troop withdrawals in the course of the year.
